draft.title: The environment as a global issue
card: Some environmental harm does not stop at a border. Air, oceans, rivers and wildlife move across the lines between countries.
Pollution
Harmful substances released in one country can spread to others. Smoke can travel through the air, and waste can be carried by ocean currents.
Climate change
Greenhouse gases mix through the whole atmosphere. Where they are released does not decide where the warming is felt.
Loss of species
Migratory animals, such as some birds and whales, travel across many countries and oceans. Harm to their habitat in one place can reduce their numbers everywhere.
draft.remember: Environmental harm can cross borders, so one country acting alone cannot fix it.

a.q: Why is climate change described as a global issue?
opts: Greenhouse gases mix in the air and affect many countries
It is caused only by countries with the largest populations
One country can stop it if that country acts strongly enough
It affects only the countries that release greenhouse gases
a.why: Greenhouse gases spread through the whole atmosphere, so the effects are not limited to where they are released. The option saying only the releasing countries are affected is tempting, but it is wrong because the warming is shared.
a.clue: Think about where released gases end up.

b.q: A mining company in Country X dumps waste into a river that flows into Country Y. Country Y bans all dumping inside its own borders. Why is this unlikely to stop the harm?
opts: The waste is released upstream, outside Country Y's control
The ban shows that dumping does not harm rivers
The river will clean itself once Country Y acts
Rivers cannot carry pollution across borders
b.why: The pollution begins in Country X, so a ban by Country Y does not reach the source. Pollution can cross borders by water, which is why one country acting alone often cannot solve the problem.
b.clue: Where does the waste enter the river?

a.best: Greenhouse gases mix in the air and affect many countries

b.best: The waste is released upstream, outside Country Y's control

problems.detail: The card says 'some' environmental harm crosses borders, but the remember line states flatly that one country acting alone 'cannot' fix it. Why (b) more carefully says 'often cannot'. Soften to 'often cannot fix it alone' to match the card.

The distractors are implausible for Year 12 HSC. 'Rivers cannot carry pollution across borders' contradicts the stem itself, and 'the river will clean itself' is obviously wrong, so the question tests very little.

b.q: A mining company in Country X dumps waste into a river that flows into Country Y. Country Y bans dumping within its own borders, but the harm goes on. What does this case best show?
opts: Harm from one country can reach another beyond its control
Pollution harms only the country where it is released
A ban inside one country can stop harm from upstream
Rivers can spread harm, but air and oceans keep it local
b.why: The waste enters the river in Country X, so Country Y's ban does not reach the source, and the harm still flows across the border. The option about a ban stopping upstream harm is tempting, but the case shows the opposite: one country acting alone often cannot solve a problem that starts elsewhere.
b.clue: Can Country Y's ban reach where the waste enters the river?

b.best: Harm from one country can reach another beyond its control
